content:
Professional indemnity insurance concerns claims for harm connected with declared professional services and errors for which the contract provides protection. For a specialist or company in Moldova, the main question is whether the work actually performed matches the activity recorded in the policy. A profession's name alone does not always describe every service provided.

This material helps consultants, designers and other service businesses prepare questions for an individual assessment. It does not establish that every profession, error or contract is eligible. Legal duties applying to a particular profession and insurance conditions must be checked separately. Availability for the specific circumstances needs confirmation before a quotation.

Describe the service for which you take responsibility

Start with what you deliver to the client: a design, analysis, inspection, recommendation or continuing service. Explain who signs the result, who checks it and where it is used. A company preparing documents does not automatically have the same risk as a company also making decisions for its client.

Include relevant secondary activities, subcontracting and new services. Use a clear description rather than only an activity code or qualifications. Ask for confirmation of the accepted activity in the proposal. If an operation has not been assessed, keep that question open instead of assuming the policy's general name includes it.

A professional error is not every commercial disagreement

The MOLDCARGO page cited in the Romanian original describes professional liability in connection with errors and negligence. When reviewing your business, distinguish an alleged error from a dispute over price or commercial results. Understand a complaint through the facts, service and alleged harm, not just the tone of the message.

Explain your controls, such as review by another specialist, client approval and version records. They help describe the activity but do not automatically establish the absence of liability. Legal classification and acceptance of a claim are not decided by this article or a preliminary commercial conversation.

Distinguish the individual, company and collaborators

Identify who enters into the service agreement and who performs the work: a specialist, company, employees or external collaborators. Ask which insured persons and services can be considered under the proposal. Working on the same project does not, by itself, confirm inclusion.

For subcontracting, describe the delegated operations and how their results are checked. Review the collaborator's documents separately from your obligations to the client. A partner's policy does not establish protection for your company against every claim connected with a shared project.

Read the client contract alongside the insurance proposal

Extract the agreement's insurance requirements: activity, requested limit, period and territory. Explain whether documents are required before work starts or at every renewal. A client's requirement is a contractual issue; do not automatically present it as a legal duty for every Moldovan company.

Result guarantees, penalties, indemnities and obligations to other parties need separate attention before signing. An amount your business agrees to pay under a commercial contract does not become an accepted professional indemnity expense solely because you agreed to it.

Build a timeline of work, error, claim and notification

Record when work was performed, delivered, when the problem emerged and when messages arrived. Ask which contractual mechanism determines the relevant period for considering a claim. Definitions and time triggers may differ and must be explained in the actual proposal, not borrowed from another product.

If documents mention a retroactive date or notification period, request an example using your company's timeline. When changing insurers, compare the old and new periods. Buying a new policy does not confirm protection for an already known error, complaint or circumstance. Disclose existing situations accurately through a confidential channel.

Which harm and expenses are being considered?

Separate damage to property, injury to a person and a client's alleged financial loss. Ask which categories are accepted and what connection with the professional service is required. The word loss can refer to very different issues. A list on a public page cannot replace a proposal's definitions and exclusions.

Ask separately about defence costs, expert assessments and settlement expenses. Establish who approves appointing a lawyer, on which conditions and within which limit. Do not assume every legal invoice will be reimbursed. Check whether these costs reduce the amount available for compensation or have a separate contractual treatment.

Compare limits and excess on the same basis

A limit is the contractual ceiling, not a promise to pay every claim in full. Ask about a per-claim limit and a total limit for the insured period if the documents distinguish them. Explain whether several clients rely on the same project or working method.

The excess or deductible is the part of a loss borne by the insured under the conditions. Request an explicitly hypothetical calculation for the circumstances that concern you. Comparison is meaningful only when activities, people, periods and accepted expenses match. A lower price alone does not demonstrate equivalent protection.

Work for clients in other countries

A Moldovan company may have international clients, but the territory of work and accepted jurisdictions need clarification. Explain where services are performed, where the results are used and which court the client contract identifies. Do not automatically apply foreign policy conditions to services supplied from Moldova.

For remote work, describe the real approval and delivery process. If software, data or computer incidents are relevant, ask about the boundary with cyber risks. Professional liability, equipment protection and data security have different subjects. One project may need several assessments without automatic inclusion under one policy.

Test a proposal against a working example

Create a hypothetical example close to your services: after a document is delivered, the client alleges that incorrect information caused a loss. Record the agreed service, delivered version, approvals and date of the first complaint. Ask how the definitions relate to those facts without requesting a compensation promise.

Compare a case where the complaint concerns only late delivery and another where somebody later changed the result. Differences reveal overlooked questions. Keep written answers and identify the condition behind each explanation. The example is a learning aid, not an assessed real claim.

Maintain a professional archive after delivery

Specify where orders, contracts, deliverables and acknowledgements are stored. For each project, identify the version actually delivered, not simply the newest file on a computer. Limit access to people who need the documents under the rules applying to your activity.

An orderly archive helps establish chronology without reconstructing it from memory. Do not infer a universal retention period from this article: professional duties, data protection and contracts require separate checks. Archive management is an operational measure, not an invented insurance condition or proof that every claim will be accepted.

A useful submission without unnecessary sensitive documents

  • Services and their share of the business.
  • The person or company signing client contracts.
  • Client types, projects and relevant countries.
  • How deliverables are reviewed and approved.
  • Subcontractors and their operations.
  • Contractual insurance requirements and requested periods.
  • Claims history and known circumstances.
  • Questions about limits, excess and defence costs.

Aggregated descriptions and anonymized contract examples may suffice initially. Do not upload client files, medical details, trade secrets or passwords to a public form. Agree the final information list and transmission channel for the specific review. Keep document versions and received confirmations.

Handling a complaint already received

Record the message's date and contents, identify the relevant service and preserve original documents. Avoid retrospectively changing deliverables without a change record. Consult notification instructions in the existing policy and obtain necessary legal support. The broker does not replace the insurer in deciding acceptance and settlement.

At renewal, discuss new activities and portfolio changes. A firm moving from small assignments to complex services should be described as it operates today. Reusing an old questionnaire automatically may leave important gaps. Compare conditions before expiry and distinguish confirmed terms from requested terms.

Frequently asked questions

Is professional indemnity the same as D&O?

No. A professional service delivered to a client and the performance of a management role require different assessments. Identify the activity and person concerned by the claim.

Is it compulsory for every service company?

Do not infer a general duty from a product name. Check the law applying to the profession separately from the client's contractual requirements.

Does a new policy resolve an old complaint?

Do not assume so. Present the timeline and known circumstances, then request an assessment of the relevant conditions and periods.

How much does professional indemnity insurance cost?

Request an assessment based on the declared services, portfolio, periods and limits. Another profession's or insurer's tariff does not establish the price for your circumstances.
